metadata.author: Greg Paskal
metadata.description: PCI DSS security headers compliance finding template with comprehensive guidance for all audiences including HTTP security header implementation, HTTPS enforcement, secure cookie configuration, and infrastructure hardening to meet Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard requirements for protecting cardholder data.

EXECUTIVE.summary: Your payment application lacks required PCI DSS security headers, exposing the company to payment processor termination, failed audits, fines up to $500K per incident, and liability for payment card fraud resulting from non-compliance.
EXECUTIVE.businessRisk: Critical risk of losing payment processing ability and massive financial liability. PCI DSS non-compliance consequences: payment processor termination (cannot process cards), fines $5,000-$500,000 per incident, liability for fraud losses (millions), forensic audit costs ($50K-$500K), card brand fines (Visa/Mastercard $50K-$500K monthly), reputation damage, customer trust loss, inability to accept online payments. Data breach costs: average $4.24M per breach (IBM 2023), PLUS card replacement costs ($3-5 per card), fraud losses, regulatory fines. Criminal prosecution possible for gross negligence. Business cannot legally process payments without PCI compliance. E-commerce loses 100% payment capability. Affects: merchants accepting cards, payment service providers, e-commerce platforms, SaaS with payments. Even single breach ends business for many companies.
EXECUTIVE.complianceImpact: PCI DSS 4.0 Requirement 4.2: Strong cryptography during transmission over open networks. Requirement 6.5.10: Protect against common coding vulnerabilities (missing security headers). Requirement 11.3: Penetration testing identifies missing headers. Quarterly ASV scans flag non-compliance. Annual PCI audits (SAQ, ROC) will fail. Payment processors require compliance attestation. Cannot pass PCI certification without security headers. Loss of compliance = cannot process payments.

PROJECT_MANAGER.summary: Missing PCI DSS required security headers will cause failed PCI audits and payment processor termination. Must implement HTTPS enforcement, HSTS, secure cookies, and protective headers immediately for any payment processing application.
PROJECT_MANAGER.timeline: IMMEDIATE if processing payments. CANNOT delay - payment processors will terminate service. Implementation takes 4-8 hours for basic compliance, 2-3 days for comprehensive hardening including infrastructure. Block all payment processing until compliant if currently non-compliant.
PROJECT_MANAGER.effort: 4-8 hours: Configure security headers (2 hours), enforce HTTPS (1 hour), secure cookies (1 hour), test payment flow (2 hours), documentation (2 hours). Additional if needed: TLS 1.2+ upgrade (4-8 hours), infrastructure hardening (1-2 days), penetration testing (1 week), PCI audit preparation (2-4 weeks). Ongoing: quarterly vulnerability scans, annual audits, continuous monitoring.

DEVELOPER.summary: Application lacks HTTP security headers required by PCI DSS for protecting cardholder data during transmission. Must implement HTTPS with HSTS, secure cookie attributes, CSP, X-Frame-Options, and other protective headers.
DEVELOPER.technical: PCI DSS 4.0 security header requirements: 1) HTTPS/TLS 1.2+ for ALL pages handling cardholder data (CHD). 2) Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) to prevent protocol downgrade. 3) Secure cookie attributes (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite) for session cookies. 4) Content-Security-Policy to prevent XSS attacks. 5) X-Frame-Options to prevent clickjacking. 6) X-Content-Type-Options to prevent MIME sniffing. 7) Referrer-Policy to prevent data leakage. Required headers for PCI compliance: Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload (REQUIRED). Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none' (RECOMMENDED). X-Frame-Options: DENY or SAMEORIGIN (REQUIRED). X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff (REQUIRED). Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin (RECOMMENDED). Session cookies MUST have: Secure flag (HTTPS only), HttpOnly flag (no JavaScript access), SameSite=Strict or Lax (CSRF protection). HTTPS enforcement: redirect ALL HTTP to HTTPS, no mixed content, TLS 1.2+ only, strong cipher suites. PCI scope: any page displaying/processing/storing CHD, payment forms, checkout pages, account pages with saved cards, APIs handling payment data. Implementation: web server headers (Nginx, Apache), application headers (Spring Security, Express), CDN headers (CloudFront). Testing: SSL Labs scan (A+ rating required), Security Headers scan, PCI ASV scan, penetration testing.
DEVELOPER.vulnerability: CWE-319 (Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information) - transmitting CHD without encryption violates PCI DSS. CWE-614 (Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute) - session hijacking risk. Missing headers create: session hijacking vulnerability, XSS attack vectors, clickjacking risks, protocol downgrade attacks, MITM attack vectors. PCI DSS Requirement 6.5.10: Applications must protect against common vulnerabilities including those preventable by security headers.

SECURITY_ENGINEER.summary: Missing PCI DSS required security headers violate payment card security standards, creating vulnerability to session hijacking, XSS, clickjacking, and protocol downgrade attacks targeting cardholder data.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.vulnerability: CWE-319, CWE-614 - Missing protective headers required by PCI DSS. Specific vulnerabilities: 1) No HSTS = protocol downgrade to HTTP (CHD transmitted cleartext). 2) Insecure cookies = session hijacking (attacker steals authenticated session). 3) No CSP = XSS attacks on payment forms (inject malicious scripts). 4) No X-Frame-Options = clickjacking (trick user into clicking hidden payment button). 5) No secure cookies = cookie theft over HTTP. Each vulnerability can expose cardholder data, violating PCI DSS fundamental requirement to protect CHD during transmission.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.attackVector: 1) Protocol downgrade attack: attacker strips HTTPS, forces HTTP, intercepts CHD in cleartext. 2) Session hijacking: steal session cookie over HTTP, impersonate user, access saved cards. 3) XSS injection: inject script on payment page, steal card details as user types. 4) Clickjacking: overlay invisible payment form, trick user into submitting payment. 5) MITM attack: intercept traffic without HSTS/TLS, capture CHD. These attacks are documented, well-known, and actively exploited. PCI DSS mandates protection against these vectors.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.threatLevel: CRITICAL (COMPLIANCE) - Not theoretical - these attacks happen daily against payment systems. Missing headers = guaranteed PCI audit failure. Financial impact: $100K-$5M per breach (card replacement, fraud, fines, forensics). Operational impact: payment processing termination, forensic audit, potential business closure. Legal impact: liability for fraud, regulatory fines, criminal prosecution for gross negligence. Reputation impact: customer loss, media coverage, trust damage.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.mitigationUrgency: IMMEDIATE - cannot process payments without compliance. Stop all payment processing if currently non-compliant. Implementation timeline: 1-2 days for emergency fix, 1 week for full compliance, 4 weeks for audit readiness. Zero tolerance for delay - payment processors will terminate non-compliant merchants. Prioritize: 1) HTTPS enforcement (day 1). 2) HSTS implementation (day 1). 3) Secure cookies (day 1). 4) Protective headers (day 2). 5) Penetration testing (week 1). 6) ASV scan (week 2).

OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.summary: Infrastructure must enforce HTTPS, implement security headers, configure TLS 1.2+, secure cookies, and enable logging/monitoring to meet PCI DSS requirements for payment processing environments.
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.technical: PCI DSS infrastructure requirements: 1) TLS 1.2 or 1.3 ONLY (disable SSL, TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1). 2) Strong cipher suites (disable weak ciphers). 3) Valid certificates (no self-signed, no expired). 4) HTTPS enforcement (HTTP redirects, HSTS). 5) Security headers on ALL responses. 6) Secure session management (encrypted, httpOnly, secure cookies). 7) Network segmentation (separate payment processing). 8) Firewall rules (restrict access). 9) Logging/monitoring (all access to CHD). 10) Intrusion detection/prevention. Required headers: Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload. Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; upgrade-insecure-requests. X-Frame-Options: DENY. X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin. Cookie configuration: Set-Cookie: session_id=xxx; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/; Max-Age=1800. Implementation points: Load balancer/ALB (TLS termination, header injection), Web server (Nginx/Apache headers), Application (framework security settings), CDN (CloudFront security headers). Testing: SSL Labs (A+ required), Security Headers scan, PCI ASV scan (quarterly), penetration test (annually).
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.scope: ALL infrastructure in payment processing scope (cardholder data environment - CDE): web servers handling payment pages, application servers processing payments, databases storing CHD (if applicable), load balancers, firewalls, network infrastructure, payment gateway connections, third-party integrations. Segmentation: isolate CDE from non-CDE systems, restrict network access, implement DMZ, separate databases. Must apply to: production (critical), staging (important for testing), development (if using real CHD - should never happen).
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.monitoring: PCI DSS monitoring requirements: 1) Log ALL access to cardholder data. 2) Monitor security header presence (continuous). 3) Alert on TLS/cipher issues. 4) Track failed authentication attempts. 5) Monitor for protocol downgrade. 6) File integrity monitoring (FIM). 7) Intrusion detection (IDS/IPS). 8) Vulnerability scanning (quarterly ASV). Specific monitoring: SSL/TLS certificate expiration (alert 30 days prior), security header presence (every response), HTTPS redirect functioning, cookie security attributes, CSP violations, clickjacking attempts. Logging retention: 3+ months online, 1+ year archived. Use SIEM for centralized logging. Implement real-time alerting for security anomalies.

QA_TESTER.summary: PCI DSS compliance testing requires validation of HTTPS enforcement, security headers, secure cookies, payment flow security, and vulnerability scanning to verify protection of cardholder data.
QA_TESTER.testImplication: Cannot validate PCI compliance without comprehensive security testing. Must test: HTTPS enforcement (all pages redirect), HSTS header present (verify with Security Headers tool), secure cookie attributes (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite), all protective headers present (CSP, X-Frame-Options, etc.), TLS 1.2+ only (verify with SSL Labs), no mixed content (all resources over HTTPS), payment form security (no JavaScript access to card fields), session management (timeout, secure transmission). Specialized testing: ASV scan (quarterly by approved vendor), penetration testing (annually by QSA), code review (secure coding practices), vulnerability assessment. Testing tools: SSL Labs, Security Headers, OWASP ZAP, Burp Suite, PCI ASV scanners.
QA_TESTER.riskIfNotFixed: Failed PCI audit - cannot process payments. Payment processor termination - lose payment capability. Fines $5K-$500K per incident. Data breach liability - millions in fraud losses. Card brand fines - $50K-$500K monthly. Forensic audit costs - $50K-$500K. Reputation damage - customer loss. Legal liability - lawsuits. Criminal prosecution - gross negligence. Business closure - cannot survive without payments. Insurance non-coverage - breach not covered. Enterprise customer loss - require PCI compliance.

nginx.testCode:
# Test PCI DSS headers

# Test HSTS
curl -I https://payment.example.com | grep -i strict-transport-security

# Test X-Frame-Options
curl -I https://payment.example.com | grep -i x-frame-options

# Test all headers
curl -I https://payment.example.com

# Test HTTPS redirect
curl -I http://payment.example.com

# Test TLS version (should only allow TLS 1.2+)
openssl s_client -connect payment.example.com:443 -tls1_1
# Should fail

openssl s_client -connect payment.example.com:443 -tls1_2
# Should succeed
nginx.dependencies:
# Nginx with SSL module
sudo apt-get install nginx-full

verificationSteps: 1. Verify HTTPS enforced (all HTTP redirects to HTTPS)
2. Test HSTS header: curl -I https://domain.com | grep Strict-Transport-Security
3. Verify TLS 1.2+ only: openssl s_client -connect domain.com:443 -tls1_1 (should fail)
4. Test all security headers with Security Headers scanner
5. Verify secure cookie attributes (Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite)
6. Run SSL Labs scan (must achieve A+ rating)

tls-config.config:
# TLS Configuration for PCI DSS Compliance

# OpenSSL cipher suite string (PCI DSS approved)
ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES256-SHA384:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-SHA256

# Protocols: TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 ONLY
# Disable: SSL, TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1

# Certificate requirements:
# - Valid (not self-signed)
# - Not expired
# - 2048-bit RSA or 256-bit ECC minimum
# - SHA-256 signature
# - Subject Alternative Name (SAN) for all domains
tls-config.reload:
# Reload web server after TLS changes
sudo systemctl reload nginx
tls-config.verify:
# Test with SSL Labs
curl https://www.ssllabs.com/ssltest/analyze.html?d=your-domain.com

# Must achieve A+ rating for PCI DSS

OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.rollbackPlan:
1. Backup all configuration files before changes
2. Test in staging with payment gateway test mode
3. If HTTPS breaks application:
   - Check certificate validity
   - Verify TLS configuration
   - Check mixed content issues
4. If headers break functionality:
   - CSP: adjust directives gradually
   - X-Frame-Options: verify no legitimate iframe usage
5. Keep HTTP->HTTPS redirect functional
6. Cannot rollback to non-compliance - fix issues forward
7. Payment processor will terminate if non-compliant
verificationSteps: 2. Security Headers scan (all PCI headers present)
3. PCI ASV scan (quarterly by approved vendor)

manualTests.name: HTTPS Enforcement Test
steps: 3. Check URL bar shows padlock icon
